title: Distance bands gave no clear M6+ share contrast after shallow M7 to below M8 earthquakes in ComCat, 2001-2024
abstract: We tested whether nearby events have a larger size share after shallow M7 to below M8 earthquakes. We used a fixed global ComCat M5.5+ snapshot and days 1 to 30 within 300 km. We compared the M6+ share within 100 km with the share at 100-300 km, within each sequence and exact preferred magnitude type. Of 217 eligible centers, 26 supplied 34 matched groups with 329 events. The weighted near-minus-far contrast was +6.46 percentage points. The 95% interval from resampling groups of overlapping sequences was -5.39 to +15.24 points. Thus the primary test gave no clear size contrast. All six planned checks also had intervals that included zero. The 2013-2024 point estimate had the opposite sign. A separate implementation confirmed event selection and the primary estimate. Few matched sequences, changing catalogs, mixed sources, background events and epicentral distance in place of fault distance limit inference. The result does not establish a size law or a stress gradient. Code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and reproduction steps are included. Source records remain external.

display.caption: Near-minus-far larger-event shares after matching each sequence and preferred magnitude type. Bars give 95% intervals from 10000 resamples of groups of overlapping sequences. Every interval includes zero. The checks are not independent tests.

citations.reason: This prior conditional-size test motivated the question. We reuse its public source snapshot, but no code or result table. Samples overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
